correctness.rationale: A ladder spanning tree is determined by a nonempty ordered rung set and one missing horizontal edge between successive rungs. Its degree-three vertex count is L-2. Inspected local marks 0,+,- and transfer B(u) with gap lengths 1,2,>=3; endpoint factors and one-rung term ensure all n>=1. Rational transfer yields displayed P_n(z) series with denominator 1-(z+3)u+(3-2z)u^2-(2z^2-3z+1)u^3. Independent exact symbolic expansion checked P1=1, P2=4, P3=8+6z+z^2, P4=14+28z+14z^2 and P5=22+84z+87z^2+16z^3, total counts matching 1/(1-4u+u^2). At z=1 the dominant simple pole 2-sqrt(3) and analytic separation give quasi-powers, exact mean density 2sqrt(3)-3 and variance 92sqrt(3)/3-53>0, hence CLT. Finite n enumeration alone was not treated as the CLT proof.

originality.rationale: Klenke 2017 primary work gives rung renewal and uniform missing-rail-edge positions but not the evaluated leaf-marked generating function or mean/variance constants. Gantert-Klenke 2023 focuses on random walks on random ladder trees, whose CLT is for walk displacement, not leaf-count. General joint degree formulas could in principle generate the distribution but do not report its evaluated rational expression and asymptotic constants. Resultary search found other family leaf distributions, not ladder-specific equivalence. Best-of-knowledge PASS with residual implicit-coverage risk.
